_meta.deliverable: 0.7 input: how x and y are paired
how_to_read: PISA is cross-sectional: no student is observed twice. We follow GROUPS instead (a pseudo-panel, Deaton 1985).
For each enabled pair, each country c and each group g: x = representative state vector of (c, g) in the 'from' cycle, y = the same group's vector in the 'to' cycle.
x and y share the same n state factors (factor_dict.json, role 'state'), so M is square (n x n), which Phase 4 needs for eigen-analysis.
Columns of X and Y are stacked over pairs, countries and groups: X, Y are n x N. Phase 1 solves M_G X = Y over the 'global' pairs; Phase 2 fits Delta M on the 'philippines' pairs.
A pair is used only if enabled AND both cycles are in config cycles.years AND both files are set in config paths.raw_files (imple.config.transition_pairs / available_cycles).

International files for 2000-2015 exist too. To use them, add the years to cycles.years, add their column names in config columns, and add pairs here; most attitudinal indices are named or scaled differently before 2018.
_meta.interpretation: M maps a group's situation at one cycle to its situation one cycle later, an approximate 'one-cycle step' of the educational trajectory.
_meta.years_between_cycles_note: 2018 to 2022 is 4 years (2021 was postponed by COVID-19); 2022 to 2025 is 3. Use 'years' to normalise if per-year rates are needed.

global.notes: Includes the COVID-19 disruption for every country.

philippines.notes: Delta M from this pair also absorbs the PH-specific pandemic shock (one of the longest school closures worldwide); state this in the limitations.
Second PH pair. Fitting M_PH on each pair separately gives the cycle-to-cycle consistency check in Phase 3.4.

validation.notes: Phase 3.5 held-out accuracy: refit M_G without one country, predict that country's y from x, repeat.
